column1: # CHASING GERDA'S MARRIAGE FOR HER FATHER — AND THE ROUTE IS CLOSED, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYBODY TRIES IT.
# Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA, 9 October 2026.
# WHY HER. GERDA FELICITAS BADE née LEIBHOLZ, died 15 February 1993, Sterberegister Wilmersdorf 1993
# Nr. 312, is the only one of the seven documented Leibholz who points UPWARD. She was BORN a Leibholz
# and married out, so she had Leibholz parents in Berlin within living memory — and the marriage that
# made her a Bade should name her father.
field
# ---------------- WHAT WAS CHECKED FIRST, AND IT RESHAPED THE JOB ----------------
*** THE CLOSURE PERIODS, READ OUT OF THE CATALOGUE RATHER THAN OFF A NOTE ***
column2: Enumerated office by office across the whole of LABSA: *** BIRTHS STOP AT 1914 — 209 volumes, 14.8 GB. MARRIAGES STOP AT 1944 — 313 volumes, 28.3 GB. *** The September reading holds: 110 years for a birth, 80 for a marriage, the window moving forward one year at a time.

column1: AND IF SHE WAS BORN IN 1914 OR EARLIER THE BIRTH ENTRY IS BETTER THAN THE MARRIAGE
column2: a birth entry names both parents outright. A MARRIAGE ENTRY MAY NOT: this archive established on 29 September, from the 1924 Leibholz–Luwinski entry, that the 1920s Prussian form NAMES NO PARENTS AT ALL and cites each party's birth register instead. So the marriage might hand over a citation rather than a name — still useful, but not the thing asked for.

column1: *** AND A TRAP THIS ARCHIVE WALKED INTO AND SHOULD NOT AGAIN ***
column2: querying births for "Standesamt Wedding von Berlin", "Mitte von Berlin", "Tiergarten von Berlin", "Schöneberg" and "Neukölln" RETURNS NOTHING — and that zero means nothing. THOSE BOROUGH REGISTRY OFFICES DID NOT EXIST BEFORE 1938. A pre-1914 Berlin birth is under the OLD names: Standesamt Berlin I to XIII, Rixdorf I-III, Charlottenburg I-IV, and the rest. THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY KNEW THAT AND HAD FORGOTTEN IT — Kurt's own birth is STANDESAMT BERLIN VIII, Prenzlauer Berg. Anyone sweeping "Neukölln births" for a 1910 child gets a confident zero from an office that did not exist.

column1: # ---------------- WHY THE MARRIAGE CANNOT BE CHASED FROM HERE ----------------
*** EVERY MARRIAGE VOLUME TESTED IS COMPLETELY BLIND ***
column2: Four sampled across two offices and three decades — Schöneberg 1940-41 (338 pp), Schöneberg 1942-43 (317 pp), Charlottenburg I 1916-20 (382 pp), Charlottenburg I 1935-38 (171 pp). *** ALL FOUR SCORE 0.0 CONTROL NAMES A PAGE. NOT A THIN TEXT LAYER — NO TEXT AT ALL. *** The whole pre-1944 marriage run is image-only.

column1: SO THE ARITHMETIC KILLS IT
column2: 313 VOLUMES, EVERY ONE READ BY EYE, WITH NO BOROUGH AND NO YEAR TO NARROW BY. At the four to six image reads a volume this archive's method costs, that is on the order of FIFTEEN HUNDRED READS for one woman. THAT IS NOT A SEARCH, IT IS A GESTURE, and it is not being done.

column1: and nothing available narrows it
column2: she died in Wilmersdorf but that says nothing about where she married; the surname BADE is common; and no birth year is held, so even the decade is open. A SWEEP NEEDS A BOROUGH OR A YEAR AND THERE IS NEITHER.

column1: # ---------------- THE ONE THING THAT WOULD HAVE NARROWED IT, CHECKED AND ABSENT ----------------
HER OWN INDEX ENTRY CARRIES NO BIRTH DATE
column2: P Rep. 570 Nr. 3306 was downloaded and both her entries opened — page 7 under B, "Bade geb. Leibholz, Gerda Felicitas, 15.02.1993 · 312", and page 74 under L, "Leibholz, Gerda Felicitas, 15.02.1993 · 312". THE COLUMNS ARE NAME, DEATH DATE, RELIGION AND REGISTER NUMBER. There is no birth date in the series.

column1: *** AND THE IMAGE CANNOT CONFIRM HER, WHICH REVERSES THE USUAL RULE ***
column2: the page scan is a FAINT, DEGRADED PHOTOCOPY and her line is barely resolvable at full resolution. For these 1993 volumes THE TEXT LAYER IS NOT OCR OF THAT SCAN — it is a clean born-digital transcription supplied with the volume, and it is the BETTER WITNESS. This archive's standing rule is that the image settles what the text layer only suggests; here it is the other way round, and the register entry says so rather than pretending to an image confirmation it does not have.

column1: what does corroborate her
column2: THE DOUBLE INDEX. She is entered twice, under her married name on page 7 and her birth name on page 74, with THE SAME REGISTER NUMBER 312 from two unrelated positions sixty-seven pages apart. That is the series checking itself, and it is the same control that validated the Spandau 1993 pairing at 2,394 of 2,396.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT ACTUALLY ANSWERS THE QUESTION ----------------
*** ORDER THE DEATH ENTRY, NOT THE MARRIAGE: STERBEREGISTER WILMERSDORF 1993 NR. 312 ***
column2: A MODERN GERMAN DEATH ENTRY NAMES THE DECEASED'S PARENTS. It also gives the birth date and birthplace. SO THE CERTIFICATE PROBABLY ANSWERS "WHO WAS GERDA'S FATHER" DIRECTLY AND MAKES THE MARRIAGE UNNECESSARY — and if it does not, it supplies the birth date and birthplace that would make a birth-index or marriage-index search narrow enough to run. Orderable by number through service.berlin.de. *** A PURCHASE, AND DAVID'S TO MAKE. ***

column1: and it is the cheapest of the four certificates now outstanding
column2: Wilmersdorf 1993 Nr. 312 (Gerda, her father) · Kreuzberg 1948 Nr. 2493 (Heinrich, and Agnes as surviving widow) · Wilmersdorf 1983 Nr. 304 (Hilde) · Tiergarten 1974 Nr. 1160 (Ella) · Tempelhof 1982 Nr. 161 (Charlotte). THE FIRST TWO ARE THE ONES THAT REACH A NEW GENERATION; the other three only confirm identifications already made.
